presentationType.clinicalPrompt: Red-flag screen. Classify the overall presentation before any nerve-specific triage: a palpable mass, an acute traumatic injury, typical compressive/neuropathic symptoms, or genuinely unclear.
presentationType.patientQuestion: Which of these best describes what is going on right now?
presentationType.extractionHints: Map to "mass_lump" for any mention of a lump, bump, swelling, knot, or growth they can feel. Map to "acute_trauma" for a recent injury, cut, accident, fall, fracture, or "it happened suddenly after X". Map to "typical_nerve_symptoms" for ongoing pins-and-needles, numbness, shooting pain, or weakness without a lump or recent injury. Use "unsure" only when the text is too vague to place.

dominantSymptom.clinicalPrompt: The single most bothersome symptom, used to weight the differential between compressive pain, sensory loss, motor loss, or a mixed picture.
dominantSymptom.extractionHints: Choose "pain" for aching, burning, shooting, or electric pain as the chief complaint. Choose "numbness_tingling" for numb, asleep, pins-and-needles, or tingling. Choose "weakness" for dropping things, a weak grip, foot drop, or muscles "not working". Choose "mixed" when two or more are described as equally dominant.

symptomLocation.clinicalPrompt: Primary anatomical territory of the symptoms. The main anatomical router: upper limb vs lower limb vs neck-radiating drives which sub-specialty sees the patient.
symptomLocation.patientQuestion: Where do you feel it the most?
symptomLocation.extractionHints: Map to "arm_hand" for fingers, thumb, hand, wrist, forearm, or elbow. Map to "leg_foot" for foot, toes, ankle, calf, leg, or thigh. Map to "neck_radiating" when symptoms start in the neck or shoulder and shoot/travel down into the arm. If both an arm and the neck are mentioned with radiation, prefer "neck_radiating".

symptomDuration.clinicalPrompt: Time course since onset. Acute (days), subacute (weeks), or chronic (months or longer). Influences urgency and the conservative-vs-surgical decision.
symptomDuration.patientQuestion: How long has this been going on?
symptomDuration.extractionHints: Map to "acute" for hours to a few days, "just started", "since yesterday". Map to "subacute" for roughly 1–6 weeks ("a couple of weeks"). Map to "chronic" for months, years, "for as long as I can remember", or "on and off for ages". Convert any stated number into the closest bucket.

emgStatus.clinicalPrompt: Whether nerve conduction studies / EMG have been performed and, if so, the result. Pulled from the referral or medical record rather than the patient.
emgStatus.patientQuestion: Have you had a nerve test (sometimes called an EMG or a nerve conduction study) — and if so, what did they tell you?
emgStatus.extractionHints: Map to "not_done" if there is no mention of EMG/NCS or the patient says they have not had one. Map to "done_normal" when a nerve test was done and reported normal/clear/unremarkable. Map to "done_abnormal" when a nerve test showed compression, entrapment, denervation, or any abnormal finding. Treat "electrodiagnostic study", "nerve conduction", and "EMG" as the same test.

urgentRedFlag.clinicalPrompt: Up-front red-flag / urgent-access screen (the center’s <72h SLA for acute nerve injury). Detect EMERGENCY presentations that must bypass full intake.
urgentRedFlag.patientQuestion: First, a quick safety check — is any of these happening?
urgentRedFlag.extractionHints: Map to "acute_trauma" for an acute injury: laceration/knife/blast, avulsion, stretch or crush (e.g. a motor-vehicle accident), an open wound with new numbness/weakness, a suspected nerve cut with a surgical wound, or an acute (recent) brachial plexus injury. Map to "mass_lump" ONLY for a mass/lump that is rapidly growing or sounds suspicious for tumour. Map to "acute" for rapidly progressive weakness, acute foot drop, or acute wrist drop, or cauda-equina-type signals. Map to "none" when there is NO such red flag.

presentationCategory.clinicalPrompt: Non-urgent overall category that steers the deep routing: a compression/entrapment picture, an older (non-acute) traumatic injury, a stable mass, a pain-predominant picture, functional loss after an upper-motor-neuron event, or genuinely unclear.
presentationCategory.patientQuestion: Which of these best fits your situation overall?
presentationCategory.extractionHints: Map to "compression" for ongoing pins-and-needles/numbness/weakness suggesting a pinched or entrapped nerve. Map to "traumatic_chronic" for symptoms following an OLD/healed injury or prior surgery. Map to "mass_stable" for a lump/mass that is stable or slowly changing. Map to "pain_predominant" when pain is by far the main problem and the cause/target is unclear. Map to "functional_umn" for loss of function AFTER a stroke, brain injury, cerebral palsy, or spinal-cord injury. Use "unclear" only when it genuinely does not fit any of these.

primarySymptom.clinicalPrompt: The single most bothersome symptom. Muscle wasting flags advanced denervation and weights toward diagnostics / surgical urgency.
primarySymptom.patientQuestion: What’s the single most bothersome part?
primarySymptom.extractionHints: Choose "pain" for aching/burning/shooting pain as the chief complaint. Choose "numbness_tingling" for numb/asleep/pins-and-needles. Choose "weakness" for dropping things, weak grip, foot drop, muscles not working. Choose "muscle_wasting" when they describe a muscle visibly shrinking, thinning, or wasting away. Choose "mixed" when two or more are equally dominant.

symptomRegion.clinicalPrompt: Detailed anatomical territory (real Duke peripheral-nerve regions). Drives the upper-vs-lower and spine-vs-peripheral routing.
symptomRegion.extractionHints: Map to "neck_radiating" when symptoms start in the neck/shoulder blade and travel down the arm. "shoulder_upper_arm" for the shoulder or upper arm. "elbow" around the elbow. "forearm" for the forearm. "wrist" at the wrist. "hand_fingers" for hand, thumb, or fingers. "hip_thigh" for hip or outer/front thigh. "knee" around the knee/outer knee. "lower_leg" for the shin/calf. "ankle_foot" for the ankle, foot, or toes. Use "multifocal" when symptoms are in several separate areas or all over.

laterality.clinicalPrompt: One side vs both. Bilateral symptoms raise suspicion for a systemic/diffuse process.
laterality.extractionHints: Map to "one_side" for left-only or right-only. Map to "both_sides" when both arms, both legs, or both sides are affected (even if one is worse).

durationBand.clinicalPrompt: Time course tied to the center’s 6–12 week referral guidance. Drives conservative-vs-surgical timing.
durationBand.patientQuestion: How long has this been going on?
durationBand.extractionHints: Map to "acute_lt2wk" for under ~2 weeks. "subacute_2_6wk" for roughly 2–6 weeks. "approaching_6_12wk" for about 6–12 weeks. "chronic_gt12wk" for more than 3 months, many months, years.

priorTraumaSurgery.clinicalPrompt: Relevant history: a prior injury, a prior surgery (post-surgical neuroma / amputation pain), or none. Steers toward reconstruction / neuroma-pain surgery.
priorTraumaSurgery.patientQuestion: Has the affected area had a previous injury or a previous surgery (including any amputation)?
priorTraumaSurgery.extractionHints: Map to "prior_surgery" for any previous operation or amputation in the area. Map to "recent_injury" for a previous (non-acute) injury to the area. Map to "none" if neither is mentioned.

nerveStudyStatus.clinicalPrompt: Whether EMG / nerve conduction studies exist and their result. Gates surgical-vs-diagnostic routing.
nerveStudyStatus.patientQuestion: Have you had a nerve test (EMG or nerve conduction study)? If so, what did it show?
nerveStudyStatus.extractionHints: Map to "not_done" if no nerve test has been done. "done_normal" if a nerve test was normal/clear. "done_abnormal" if it showed compression/entrapment/denervation/any abnormality. "unsure" if a test was done but they do not know the result.

nightOrPositional.clinicalPrompt: Night-time or position-dependent symptoms — a classic compressive/entrapment pattern.
nightOrPositional.patientQuestion: Are the symptoms worse at night or in certain positions?
nightOrPositional.extractionHints: Map to "yes" if symptoms are worse at night, wake them from sleep, or are clearly triggered by a position/posture. Map to "no" otherwise.

progression.clinicalPrompt: Trajectory: stable, slowly worsening, or rapidly worsening. Rapid worsening on the spine path escalates severity.
progression.patientQuestion: How is it changing over time?
progression.extractionHints: Map to "stable" for unchanged / waxing-and-waning. "slowly_worsening" for a gradual decline over weeks-months. "rapidly_worsening" for a fast decline over days-weeks.

functionalImpact.clinicalPrompt: How much function is lost: mild, interferes with daily activity, or severe loss. Weights surgical-candidacy and which spine surgeon.
functionalImpact.patientQuestion: How much is this affecting your daily life?
functionalImpact.extractionHints: Map to "mild" for minor/manageable. "interferes_daily" when it clearly limits work, sleep, or daily tasks. "severe_loss" for major loss of use, can't work, can't use the limb.

systemicContext.clinicalPrompt: Systemic background: diabetes or a known systemic/autoimmune condition.
systemicContext.patientQuestion: Do you have diabetes, or any known autoimmune or systemic medical condition?
systemicContext.extractionHints: Map to "diabetes" if diabetes/high blood sugar is mentioned. "autoimmune_systemic" for lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid disease, vasculitis, or another systemic/autoimmune condition. "none" if neither is mentioned.

umnHistory.clinicalPrompt: Upper-motor-neuron history (stroke / TBI / cerebral palsy / spinal-cord injury).
umnHistory.patientQuestion: Have you had a stroke, a brain injury, cerebral palsy, or a spinal-cord injury?
umnHistory.extractionHints: Map to "stroke" for a prior stroke; "tbi" for a traumatic brain injury/head injury; "cerebral_palsy" for cerebral palsy; "spinal_cord_injury" for a spinal-cord injury or paralysis from a back/neck injury. Map to "none" if none of these.
